newsitem.title: USA: CNET signs 20 partners for software sales.
newsitem.headline: CNET signs 20 partners for software sales.

text.p: CNET said it has signed agreements with 20 Internet service providers, including Sprint Corp and MCI Communications Corp, to promote its new software delivery service.
CNET said it agreed to deals related to its Download.com software service with Sprint, MCI, MindSpring Enterprises Inc, Earthlink Network Inc, Concentric Network, and other U.S. access providers.
Other partners include three Japanese Internet providers Bekkoame Internet, So-Net (Sony Communications Network), a unit of Sony Corp, and Dream Train Internet Inc.
CNET said it also agreed to partnerships with Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and South Korea's Boranet.

It also had agreed to a deal with InfiNet, a U.S. venture backed by Gannett Co Inc, Knight-Ridder Inc and Landmark Communications Inc that offers a service designed to connect newspaper readers to the Internet.
CNET said the 20 partners had agreed to give its Download.com service prominent play on their own Web sites.
Download.com, which debuted Monday, compiles the Internet's most popular free software titles, including games and Internet tools. Initially all software will be free.

A spokeswoman said CNET plans to connect the Download.com site to a transaction-based service it will introduce in early November to be called BuyDirect.com, a site where commercial software can be purchased, not just free, so-called shareware.
Under the terms of the deals, CNET's Download.com will be the exclusive softwarservice linked to the "software" buttons on each of the 20 Internet access providers Web browsers.
This will allow consumers who click the "software" button to go directly ot Download.com's site to find free software or to connect with BuyDirect.com to buy commercial software.
In return, CNET said it will pay Internet service providers a percentage of the advertising revenues generated from traffic driven to Download.com through the access providers browser software.
Download.com and the soon-to-be introduced BuyDirect.com complement CNET's existing Shareware.com site, which the company claims includes more than 200,000 free or nearly free software titles.
Shareware.com is ranked among the most visited sites on the World Wide Web.
